answer: Each identity claims one shale bed on one horizon and files a pigment band sequence for it, locking a 70-credit bond. The sequence is key-signed and bound to that bed alone. A horizon auditor recomputes the expected pigment order from the shale survey table for the bed and burns the bond on any out-of-order or duplicated band. The first filing costs 33 credits, the kth 33+6(k-1), the 1000th 6027, so 1000 fakes cost 3,030,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked bonds. Honest identities pay once. A rented-sequence ring fails: a borrowed pigment sequence matches its own bed, not the claimed shale bed.
